benchmark.category: a single-file browser campus-life game with five timed daily missions, drivable campus traffic and a cloned-voice office scene
benchmark.users: college students and judges playing on desktop and touch phones, running the five daily missions, driving around campus and talking to the office character

requirements.source_phrase: Do not change the flow of the game
requirements.statement: Every screen the game already had (start, character select, tutorial, play HUD, mission briefing, result card, pause, store) keeps its layout, copy, controls and screen order apart from the Bawalverse rename, the phone-landscape layout fix and the realism design pass, which may restyle materials, textures and panels but changes no flow
requirements.notes: Amended because the new window authorises a design pass ('make the UI UX more realistic') while forbidding flow changes; the earlier 'no redesign' wording would otherwise mark the sanctioned restyle as a violation.

requirements.source_phrase: Do not change the flow of the game or any other elements
requirements.statement: The served files carry the uploaded game's own code with changes confined to the branding strings, the phone-landscape CSS, the cloned-voice playback, the free-vehicle table and the realism style block; the mission table, world data, screen transitions and control handlers are otherwise the uploaded versions
requirements.notes: Amended so the change-scope check includes the voice, vehicle and realism work the user has since approved, and still catches an unrequested rewrite of missions, world data or handlers.

requirements.statement: In the Crowd Control mission the HUD's remaining-people count falls only when a person has physically left the circle: pressing E on a crowd member who still stands inside leaves the count unchanged, and the mission's success card appears only once the circle is empty
requirements.notes: Surface is the '/* 9. CROWD CONTROL */' section of /app/frontend/public/game/index.html (mxCrowdIn); reach it by starting mxStart('crowd') and reading the count from page.evaluate. The agent's fix claim is unverified, so the count is checked against who physically stands inside the circle, not against the code's own flag.

requirements.statement: mxCrowdIn counts every frame the people whose position lies inside the Crowd Control circle — including slapped and panicked ones — and mxFinish fires only when that count is zero, so a shove that leaves the person inside never completes the mission and a person who walks out is not counted twice
requirements.notes: The paranoid half of the frontend statement: the earlier bug was completion at a stale count, so the backend rule is the geometric count and the zero condition, checked with a person standing at the circle edge.

requirements.statement: When the player's energy reaches zero during a mission the crash card appears, and after it is continued a 'Mission failed' card is shown and the game stays frozen — the player cannot move and the mission clock does not advance — until that card is dismissed
requirements.notes: Reproduce by starting a mission (mxStart('crowd')) then setting S.en=0 or calling crashCard(), and dismiss with Space or a click; watch S.running, S.px/S.py and the mission timer behind the card.

requirements.statement: Setting S.en to 0 during a running mission sets S.running false, holds the player's position fixed and leaves the mission timer unchanged until the failed card is dismissed, after which the mission failure path runs exactly once
requirements.notes: The clock half of the reported bug: the failed card must not leave a live mission running underneath it. Sample the timer value twice a second apart while the card is up.

requirements.statement: Every mission's briefing 3★ target equals the time the mission actually requires — on day 1 the Yulu Time Trial shows 1:02 and The Recovery shows 2:05 — and the result card repeats the same target, so a run finishing at or under it is awarded 3★
requirements.notes: The user named the mismatch without naming missions; the build names Yulu (62 s × mxD = 1:02) and Recovery (125 s × mxD = 2:05). A fix only in the briefing chip while the result card keeps the old number still fails this requirement.

requirements.statement: One par value per mission is computed from its base duration (Yulu 62 s, Recovery 125 s) times the day multiplier mxD, formatted m:ss to whole seconds, and both the briefing chip and the result card read that value
requirements.notes: Rounding recorded as an assumption: base duration × mxD rounded to the nearest whole second, mm:ss format with a zero-padded seconds field. The value the star award compares against is the same computed number, so briefing and result cannot diverge.

requirements.source_phrase: make all the cars and bikes free to drive
requirements.statement: The store's Vehicles tab lists the Yulu pass, the Scooter, the Car keys and the Director's SUV as Owned at ₹0, and none of them offers or performs a purchase on that screen
requirements.notes: Store surface around SHOP_VEH / vehOwnAll (~5650-5690). Read the tab at 1920x800 and at 390x844; a row that still shows a price with a Buy button is the failure.

requirements.source_phrase: Every vehicle unlocked at no cost
requirements.statement: Every vehicle entry in SHOP_VEH carries a price of 0 with the all-owned flag set, so the lock check returns false for every vehicle id and the stored wallet balance is unchanged after any vehicle is entered
requirements.notes: The user's own definition of free: unlocked at no cost. Compare the save's wallet before and after entering each vehicle kind, not just the store display.

requirements.source_phrase: make all the cars and bikes free to drive
requirements.statement: On campus every parked car, scooter and Yulu, the Director's SUV and the parked auto can be entered with E with no lock message and no price prompt, and the wallet balance reads the same before and after each entry
requirements.notes: Enter each vehicle kind in turn (teleport with S.px/S.py where walking is slow); the assertion is both that entry happens and that no money moved.

requirements.source_phrase: make all the cars and bikes free to drive
requirements.statement: interact() enters a nearby vehicle of any kind without calling the lock path and without debiting the wallet, and the saved wallet and owned-vehicle list are identical before and after the entry
requirements.notes: Derived from the entry flow: a lock check that returns true only for the SUV or a balance debit on entry would pass a shallow screen check but fail here.

requirements.source_phrase: also can access running cars from the outter road
requirements.statement: Standing on the main road's west strip beside a moving car, auto or bike shows an 'E — take the car' hint, and pressing E puts the player inside it as a drivable vehicle, while a bus or truck beside the player offers no such hint and cannot be taken
requirements.notes: The user's answer defines the second half of 'free to drive'. Reading the road strip requires waiting for traffic (TRAF/nearTraf()); assert the hint text, the takeover and the bus/truck refusal separately.

requirements.source_phrase: also can access running cars from the outter road
requirements.statement: nearTraf() returns a moving car, auto or bike — never a bus or truck — within interaction range on the road, and jackTraf() turns that traffic object into the player's drivable vehicle; taking ten vehicles in a row raises no error and abandoned taken vehicles are reused so the vehicle list does not grow without bound
requirements.notes: The 'maximum 6' figure is the agent's internal number and is not treated as a contract; the contract is that repeated takeovers keep working with reuse and no crash, checked by taking ten vehicles and reading the live vehicle list length.

requirements.statement: The campus renders with grain and texture, soft cloud shade and sunlight, ambient occlusion on building facades, roof shading, window reflections and tree volume, and its cars show paint gloss and tinted glass, with the same buildings, roads and mission positions as before
requirements.notes: The user's answer names what must look more realistic. Judge by the rendered look and by no geometry change; screenshot at 1920x800 and 390x844.

requirements.statement: The served game builds its baked campus through the grain tile and bake pass once at world build — grain, cloud shade, sunlight, facade and roof shading, window reflections, tree volume — and draws cars with gloss and tinted glass, while no object position, collision box or mission position changes
requirements.notes: Mechanism behind the look: the bake runs at build, not per frame. Also the guard against the realism pass shifting colliders or mission dots, which the user's 'do not change the flow' line forbids.

requirements.statement: The HUD panels, buttons, sheets, pause menu, store and phone touch controls render with the new material and polished finish, and each still shows its label and still performs its action when clicked or tapped
requirements.notes: The user's answer names screens and panels. Paranoid form of 'a control exists': the restyled control must still do its thing and change its own state.

requirements.statement: The served file carries the realism style block those panels, buttons, sheets, the pause menu, the store and the touch controls draw their finish from, and that block sets no rule that hides an interactive element or disables pointer events on one
requirements.notes: Read the 'realism pass' CSS block (search that comment); a rule with pointer-events:none or zero opacity over a button is the realistic way a polish pass kills a control.

requirements.source_phrase: Do not change the flow of the game
requirements.statement: The sequence title screen → character select → play → mission briefing → mission → pause → store is the same as before the realism pass, each screen opening from its usual control, with no screen added, removed or reordered
requirements.notes: The user's explicit limit. Walk the whole path once on desktop and once on a phone and compare against the pre-change path; the risk is a polish pass that turns the play HUD into a menu-driven flow.

requirements.statement: The served file's screen transitions and button handlers (start button, character select, mission brief and start, pause, store) hold the same transitions as before the pass, with differences confined to the style block and to the vehicle and par logic
requirements.notes: 'Just improve the design' is the ceiling on the change; this reads the handlers and compares the transition set rather than the formatting.

requirements.statement: After the failed-mission card following a collapse is dismissed, the player moves again, free play resumes with no leftover mission HUD, and no second 'Mission failed' card appears for the same collapse
requirements.notes: The unstated half of the collapse fix: a card that never releases the frozen state traps the player, and a re-fired fail traps them again.

requirements.statement: Dismissing the post-collapse failed card runs the mission failure path once and clears the current mission, and the running flag returns to true only after the card is closed, so a second dismiss or a key press cannot fail the same mission twice
requirements.notes: Guards the double-fail and the permanently frozen state; read S.running and the current mission before, during and after dismissal.

requirements.statement: After entering several vehicles and reloading the page, Continue restores the game with the store still showing every vehicle Owned at ₹0 and the wallet at the same balance as before the reload
requirements.notes: Paranoid persistence on the new free-vehicle contract: a fix that unlocks vehicles only in memory loses them on reload.

requirements.statement: Vehicle ownership and the wallet balance live in the browser save and are read back after a reload, and entering a vehicle writes nothing that changes the balance, so the owned flags and the balance survive the reload
requirements.notes: There is no server in this product; the save record is the persistence layer, so compare the stored wallet and owned flags across a reload.

requirements.statement: Pressing E while driving a taken traffic vehicle leaves it parked on the road with the player back on foot beside it, the vehicle can be entered again afterwards, and the hint switches from 'E — take the car' to the exit prompt once inside
requirements.notes: The inverse of taking a car, which the user's line implies: a vehicle you can only enter is a trap. Also the control-state half — the prompt changes when the state changes.

requirements.statement: Leaving a taken vehicle returns foot movement at the vehicle's position and keeps that vehicle in the world as an ordinary car that can be entered again, creating no duplicate vehicle and leaving the player's wallet unchanged
requirements.notes: A takeover that removes the traffic car without adding a parked one, or adds a second copy on exit, breaks the reuse rule tested on the take path.

requirements.statement: At 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390 every HUD button, mission card button, panel close control and phone touch control receives its click or tap, with no grain, shade or lighting layer swallowing the input
requirements.notes: The main way a texture/lighting pass breaks a game is an overlay above the HUD; assert both that the control fires and that it looks pressed afterwards.

requirements.statement: The realism layers are canvas or CSS background elements with pointer events disabled or a stacking order below the HUD, so a click at each control's coordinates reaches that control's handler and triggers its action
requirements.notes: Check the computed z-index and pointer-events of the grain, cloud-shade and lighting layers against the HUD controls at all three viewports.

requirements.statement: In the mission briefing and on the result card the 3★ par value is fully visible at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390 — not clipped by the card edge, covered by the mission name or hidden behind the timer — and reads the same number in both places
requirements.notes: A corrected par that the player cannot read is not a fix; the phone card is the tight case, especially on the sideways layout where the mission card sits at the bottom.

requirements.statement: The briefing chip's par text and the result card's par text are rendered from the same computed value, so for the same mission and day the string in the briefing equals the string on the result card
requirements.notes: Two render sites reading one value is the mechanism; comparing the two rendered strings catches a second hard-coded number left in the result card.

requirements.statement: A mission's par equals its base duration in seconds (Yulu 62, Recovery 125) multiplied by the day multiplier mxD and rounded to the nearest whole second, and the 3★ award threshold is that same number, so a run of exactly par seconds earns 3★ and a run a second longer does not
requirements.notes: Class-1 business rule behind the user's 3★ complaint. Rounding to the nearest whole second is an assumption recorded here; it reproduces the stated day-1 values (62 s → 1:02, 125 s → 2:05) and is applied identically to briefing, result card and star award.

requirements.statement: After the realism pass the labels on the HUD panels, buttons and the store and pause sheets still meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against their new backgrounds at 1920x800 and 390x844
requirements.notes: Layout and visual class for the new surfaces: texture and translucency are the classic way a polish pass pushes small gold text below readable contrast.

requirements.statement: The colour pairs the realism style block sets for panel and button text compute to at least 4.5:1 against their backgrounds including any semi-transparent texture composited over them
requirements.notes: Compute from the declared colours and the texture's alpha when the pixel sample is unreliable on the canvas-rendered campus behind the panels.

requirements.statement: The store shows owned items, affordable items and unaffordable items in three visually distinct states, every vehicle shows the owned state and none shows the unaffordable state, and the Vehicles tab opens at 390x844 with each row readable and no horizontal scrolling
requirements.notes: UI-state class: distinct states keep a player from buying twice or thinking a free vehicle is locked; the phone tab is where the added rows most often overflow.

requirements.statement: Each store row's state is computed from the saved owned flags and the stored wallet, so a vehicle row reads owned before and after a reload and a priced row reads unaffordable exactly when the wallet is below its price
requirements.notes: State must come from the save and the wallet rather than a hard-coded list, otherwise a reload or a spent wallet makes the rows lie.

requirements.statement: Pressing Continue on a save written before this change loads the world with the same name, character, wallet, mission completion marks and office visit count, and the store then shows every vehicle as owned
requirements.notes: Data class for the new fields: the free-vehicle change adds save data, and an existing player's save is the one most likely to break Continue.

requirements.statement: A stored save record that lacks the new vehicle fields loads with all vehicles owned instead of throwing, is rewritten with those fields, and keeps the name, character, wallet, mission marks and office visit count it already held
requirements.notes: Seed an old-shaped save into the browser's storage, then load: an unguarded read of the new field blanks the start screen or resets the wallet.

requirements.statement: The grain tile and campus shading are baked once when the world is built, and during a mission at 1920x800 the game loop keeps advancing its frame counter at a playable rate with movement responding within about 100 ms after five minutes of play
requirements.notes: Performance class for the new visual layers: a texture regenerated or a gradient allocated per frame is the realistic leak, visible as a frame counter that drifts below real time during a timed mission.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns 200 with the realism style block and the free-vehicle table (every vehicle price 0 with the all-owned flag set) present in the served document, and loading the game raises no uncaught JS error or 404 for a script or stylesheet it references
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class: the change is a single static file, so a style block or flag that never reached the served copy is the realistic gap between the agent's report and the product.

requirements.statement: Standing within interaction range of an enterable vehicle shows a prompt naming the key and the vehicle, walking out of range removes it, and no prompt appears for a bus or a truck
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games show a contextual enter prompt only for vehicles the player can actually use, so nobody presses E on a bus and gets nothing.

requirements.statement: interact() selects the nearest enterable vehicle of the car, auto, bike, Yulu or SUV class within range and sets the hint text from it, skipping buses and trucks, and clears the hint when no vehicle is in range
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- the prompt is driven by the same nearest-vehicle query the entry action uses, so a hint that shows for an unenterable vehicle is a false promise.
